article_title: Activating Culturally Empathic Motivation in Diverse Students
citation: Donald E Grant Jr. & Jerell B. Hill. (2020). Activating Culturally Empathic Motivation in Diverse Students. Journal of Education and Learning, 9(5). https://doi.org/10.5539/jel.v9n5p45
title: Motivational Framework for Culturally Responsive Teaching (MFCRT) with four motivational conditions
description: The article presents the Motivational Framework for Culturally Responsive Teaching (MFCRT), developed by Wlodkowski and Ginsberg (1995), as a way to ensure relevance in education and promote intrinsic motivation. It is activated through four motivational conditions that work collectively and individually: inclusion (respect and connectedness), attitude (relevance and volition), meaning (engagement and challenge), and competence (effectiveness and authenticity). Each condition pairs criteria with an explanation of how learners experience increased intrinsic motivation, such as feeling safe and able to exhibit authenticity under inclusion.
requirements: Educators must operationalize the four conditions dynamically, both collectively and individually, to enhance intrinsic motivation to learn.
constraints: The framework is presented as adapted from Wlodkowski & Ginsberg (1995); the article reports no direct empirical test of it.
target_learners: learners from marginalized or intersectional groups
examples: The article's Table 2 lists the four conditions with criteria and explanations, adapted from Wlodkowski & Ginsberg (1995).
key_sources: Donald E Grant Jr. & Jerell B. Hill. (2020). Activating Culturally Empathic Motivation in Diverse Students. Journal of Education and Learning, 9(5). https://doi.org/10.5539/jel.v9n5p45

article_title: Teachers “finding peace in a frantic world”: An experimental study of self-taught and instructor-led mindfulness program formats on acceptability, effectiveness, and mechanisms.
citation: Montero-Marin et al. (2021). Teachers “Finding Peace in a Frantic World”: An Experimental Study of Self-Taught and Instructor-Led Mindfulness Program Formats on Acceptability, Effectiveness, and Mechanisms. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000542
title: M-FP mindfulness curriculum sequencing four understandings-and-skills themes across eight sessions with daily home practice
description: The Mindfulness: A Practical Guide to Finding Peace in a Frantic World (M-FP) curriculum is an introductory, skills-based training built on mindfulness-based cognitive therapy core elements and designed for improving well-being in the general population. It develops four sequenced themes: recognizing autopilot and bringing mindfulness to everyday present-moment experience; recognizing thoughts, emotions, sensations, and impulses while stabilizing attention; recognizing unhelpful patterns of thinking, feeling, and acting; and learning skills for keeping balanced and responding skillfully when difficulties arise. "The curriculum has eight sessions that work sequentially through these four main themes," with home practices including a daily 20-minute mindfulness practice.
requirements: Participants engage in a range of home practices that support learning, including a daily 20-minute mindfulness practice
constraints: Designed as an introductory program for the general population, applied here to secondary school teachers
examples: Both trial arms delivered this same M-FP manualized curriculum, one instructor-led in eight 90-minute weekly group sessions and one self-taught from the book with an accompanying app
key_sources: Montero-Marin et al. (2021). Teachers “Finding Peace in a Frantic World”: An Experimental Study of Self-Taught and Instructor-Led Mindfulness Program Formats on Acceptability, Effectiveness, and Mechanisms. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000542

article_title: Mathematics Formative Assessment System--Common Core State Standards: A Randomized Field Trial in Kindergarten and First Grade
citation: Laura B. Lang, Robert R. Schoen, Mark LaVenia, and Maureen Oberlin. (2014). Mathematics Formative Assessment System – Common Core State Standards: A Randomized Field Trial in Kindergarten and First Grade. SREE Spring 2014 Conference. https://sree.org
title: Mathematics Formative Assessment System (MFAS) with five key formative assessment strategies
description: The MFAS-CCSS is a system of tasks and rubrics designed to help teachers enact formative assessment as an ongoing process rather than a test. It was designed to provide teachers with tasks and rubrics to employ five key strategies: assessing understanding during instruction, identifying misconceptions and errors, examining student work, posing additional questions to elicit thinking, and obtaining guidance on next steps for instruction. The system was implemented with online professional development modules, weekly communities of instructional practice, and principal support.
requirements: Teachers complete three introductory online professional development modules and implement MFAS tasks related to the standards they are teaching
constraints: Formative assessment occurs only when the evidence of student thinking is used to adjust instruction to address gaps in knowledge related to instructional objectives
target_learning_goals: Elementary mathematics content aligned with the Common Core State Standards
examples: Treatment teachers used MFAS rubrics to evaluate student performance and differentiate instruction, and met weekly in grade-level communities of instructional practice facilitated by district lead teachers
key_sources: Laura B. Lang, Robert R. Schoen, Mark LaVenia, and Maureen Oberlin. (2014). Mathematics Formative Assessment System – Common Core State Standards: A Randomized Field Trial in Kindergarten and First Grade. SREE Spring 2014 Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED562773

article_title: Impact of integrating flipped classroom model and multi-functional camera system on practical skills and satisfaction in musculoskeletal rehabilitation education among health professional students.
citation: Zhang Ruike, Zhang Yi, Liang Liman, Liu Jinyi, Huang Minglei, Huang Rui, Aisaiti Adila, Yan Jiaqiao, Huang Tao, Ji Shuangquan. (2025). Impact of integrating flipped classroom model and multi-functional camera system on practical skills and satisfaction in musculoskeletal rehabilitation education among health professional students. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07861-w
title: Multi-functional camera system (MFCS) for live multi-angle demonstration capture
description: The MFCS is a classroom multimedia system of "a main system unit, four display screens, and five cameras", with tablet-controlled software for zooming, adjusting angles, selecting screen numbers, and switching between play, pause, and recording modes. During practical classes an assistant adjusts cameras to the instructor's requirements, for example one screen showing the overall scene and another a close-up of the area under examination, so distant students can watch demonstrations on screens instead of crowding around the instructor. Recordings can be reviewed after class from various angles.
requirements: An assistant operates the cameras during practical classes according to the instructor's requirements
constraints: The study applied it within a musculoskeletal rehabilitation practical course for rehabilitation therapy students
target_learners: third-year rehabilitation therapy students in health professional education
target_learning_goals: SOAP clinical reasoning and practical skills
examples: In the Combined Group classroom, ceiling-mounted cameras focused close-up shots of the operator while other group members observed from various screens (Fig. 1)
